title: Session Curation Templates — thoughtlog
content:
Quick log / brain dump for a lightweight session curation templates feature. Purpose: let product teams define (and ship) a small set of reusable session templates that shape context, system prompts, and policy toggles for specific user flows (support triage, code-assist, sales pitch, onboarding coach).

Why I care (problem hypothesis):
- Customers ask for ways to standardize session behaviour across product areas (so different teams don't reinvent system prompt fragments).
- Current approach: ad-hoc saved prompts + engineering glue. Results in drift, inconsistent UX, stale prompts.
- Opportunity: templates that combine policy (routing tier, model family, dedup TTL), context framing (short preambles, persona hints), and runtime knobs (max tokens, temperature presets, fidelity profiles).

Goals (initial):
- Minimal authoring surface for PMs/designers to create a template (title, description, system prompt blocks, runtime presets).
- Templates can be referenced by route id or by SDK param. SDK param should be something like {template: "sales-pitch-v1"} for fast adoption.
- Backwards-compatible: templates are additive; existing apps keep using raw prompts.
- Observe metrics per-template: latency, cost/token, response quality (eval sets) -> tied into Optimize.

Non-goals (first pass):
- Not building a full templating language (no complex branching or loops). Keep to replaceable variables and optional context slots.
- Not exposing private customer templates in public catalog.

User journeys (sketch):
- PM creates template in Console: name, description, tags, system blocks, optional variable placeholders ({{user_role}}), runtime preset dropdown (low-latency / balanced / high-quality). Save -> template id.
- Developer calls API or SDK with template id. Service expands variables from session metadata + merges with any explicit prompt overrides.
- Console shows per-template telemetry dashboard and ability to roll a template out via canary to a subset of routes.

Rough wire / API sketch:
- POST /templates -> {name, description, system_blocks: ["..."] , variables: ["company","user_role"], runtime_preset: "balanced"} -> returns template_id
- GET /templates/:id -> returns manifest
- SDK usage: redwood.generate({template: "sales-pitch-v1", template_vars: {company: "Acme"}, overrides: {temperature: 0.2}})

User stories (priority):
- As a PM, I want to create a template from a curated set of system blocks so I can ensure consistent framing across flows. (AC: can select prebuilt blocks and create new ones, saved template appears in list)
- As an engineer, I want the SDK to accept a template id so I can remove prompt construction boilerplate. (AC: simple SDK param works, fallback to raw prompt works)
- As an SRE, I want to see per-template token breakdowns so we can attribute cost. (AC: Console shows tokens/req and cost estimates per-template)
- As a UX researcher, I want to run A/B test between two templates on the same route. (AC: Console can assign 50/50 traffic split for a route between template variants)

Metrics / success signals:
- Adoption: % of new hosted-api routes referencing a template after 90 days (target 20% for pilot customers)
- Cost impact: average tokens/request change (want no >10% undesirable regressed cases)
- Quality: subjective evals on 3 prompt-sensitive flows (improve or hold steady vs baseline)
- Ops: incidents related to template resolution (target zero)

Rollout / experiment plan (small experiment):
- Pilot with 2 internal teams: support-assist and onboarding-bot. Create 3 templates: support-short, support-deep, onboarding-light.
- Observe for 2 weeks, measure token counts, latencies, user satisfaction (internal). Iterate.

Open questions / risks (quick list):
- Ownership model: who owns library? product infra or content ops? (lean content ops + product)
- Security: templates may embed system-level instructions; need RBAC + audit logs. Map to existing Private/KMS audit flows.
- Compatibility with rollouts and fallback: if template references a runtime preset not available in a region, should auto-fallback to nearest compatible preset. Spec fallback ordering.
- Variable injection surface: how to prevent template author from including PII variables that get persisted? Need clear guidance and optional auto-redaction.

Implementation notes (engineering shortcuts / naive path):
- MVP: store templates as small JSON manifests in ConfigStore (per-tenant override optional). Resolve at request-time with merge logic in runtime router. No fancy compiled DSL.
- Hook into existing telemetry: add template_id to trace span and cost attribution pipeline.
- Console: simple form-first UI. Later add a block library with search.

To-do (next steps):
- [ ] Sync with content-ops and security on RBAC + audit requirements (owner: Ava)
- [ ] Prototype server-side resolution in a dedicated branch (owner: Lucas)
- [ ] Draft SDK shim for Node and Python (owner: Noor)
- [ ] Create internal pilot templates and run 2-week pilot with Support (owner: PM: K?)

Notes to self (messy):
- Think about template versioning: template_id:v2 vs immutable id + version metadata. Prefer immutable id with explicit versions for rollouts.
- Could be integrated with existing "prompt library" idea but don't conflate in MVP. Keep simple mapping: template -> manifest -> runtime-preset
- Nice-to-have: templating preview with sample variables and live token estimate. Could reuse token-estimator component.

Slack snippets I copied here: "we could let templates own a routing tier so premium customers get high-quality preset by default" — need to check pricing implications.

Experimental UX heuristic: allow template authors to mark sections as "always visible" vs "hidden for end users" (for internal assistant context). Might help compliance.

End of dump. Will tidy into a mini-PRD once we sync with content ops and SRE.
